title: Generating Reading Comprehension Exercises with Large Language Models for Educational Applications
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of automatically generating high-quality English reading comprehension exercises for educational use. The authors argue that large language models (LLMs) have strong potential for educational text generation, but that existing work has focused more on teaching support and writing correction than on the generation of assessment content such as reading comprehension items.

To address this gap, the paper proposes Reading Comprehension Exercise Generation (RCEG), a framework that combines supervised fine-tuning, reward modeling, PPO-based reinforcement learning, and post-processing control mechanisms. The system uses task-specific datasets built from RACE and Chinese examination sources, then applies controlled decoding and a toxicity-filtering discriminator to produce reading passages, questions, answer options, and explanations that are more coherent, relevant, and pedagogically aligned.

The paper evaluates the framework using automatic text-similarity and reasoning metrics, plus human preference and toxicity-related analyses, rather than learner outcome measures. The only clearly named educational population referenced is Chinese middle school students in a cited prior study, but this paper itself is a model-development and evaluation study on benchmark datasets rather than a classroom intervention. The authors conclude that RCEG improves generated exercise quality and robustness compared with baseline models, but the evidence is about content generation quality, not direct K-12 reading or literacy gains.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A large language model-based educational content generation framework for automatically generating English reading comprehension exercises, including articles, questions, answers, explanations, and controlled candidate selection.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper proposes Reading Comprehension Exercise Generation (RCEG), a framework built on LLMs and evaluated for generating English reading comprehension exercises for educational use.

findings.finding_summary: The framework was evaluated on generated reading comprehension content, not learner achievement. Compared with baseline models, RCEG-SP improved BLEU-4 and ROUGE scores for text similarity; for example, RCEG-SPQwen2.5-3B achieved BLEU-4 = 27.23 and ROUGE-1 = 22.12, outperforming its base model and the GPT2 finetune baseline. The full RCEG pipeline also lowered perplexity on clean and toxic test sets, indicating better fluency and robustness.

On zero-shot reasoning benchmarks used as proxy evaluations, RCEG-SP improved HotpotQA and HellaSwag in several cases but showed mixed effects on ARC and ReClor. For example, Qwen2.5-1.5B improved from 27.02 to 41.39 on HellaSwag and from 89.25 to 95.25 on HotpotQA, while ARC and ReClor declined for that model.
findings.measure: FreeEval benchmark scores on ARC, ReClor, HotpotQA, HellaSwag

quality_tier_rationale: This is a framework/prototype paper evaluating generated text quality and benchmark proxy metrics, not a student-level intervention study. It does not provide direct K-12 reading or literacy outcome evidence relative to business-as-usual or non-AI supports.
impact_tier_rationale: No learner outcome effect size is reported, and the reported improvements are on generation quality and proxy reasoning benchmarks rather than K-12 reading achievement. Therefore there is no direct evidence of educational impact on reading/literacy outcomes.
